Jessica the jackrabbit wants to climb down a wall. The wall consists of 2026 horizontal layers stacked vertically. The $n$th layer from the top is partitioned into $2^n - 1$ identical rectangular bricks arranged side by side. Jessica begins in the topmost layer, which contains a single brick. A move consists of Jessica going down one layer to a brick that shares a side with the brick she is currently on.

Determine, with proof, the total number of distinct sequences of moves Jessica can take to reach the 2026th layer.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let the common width of the wall be \(1\).  
For layer \(n\), set
\[
m=2^n-1.
\]
The \(i\)-th brick in layer \(n\) has horizontal interval
\[
\left[\frac{i-1}{m},\frac{i}{m}\right].
\]

Now look at layer \(n+1\). It has
\[
2^{n+1}-1=2m+1
\]
bricks, so the \(j\)-th brick in layer \(n+1\) has horizontal interval
\[
\left[\frac{j-1}{2m+1},\frac{j}{2m+1}\right].
\]
Two bricks in consecutive layers share a side exactly when their horizontal intervals overlap in more than a point.

Fix a brick in layer \(n\). Scale the layer below by making each lower brick have width \(1\). Then the fixed brick occupies
\[
\left(\frac{i-1}{m}(2m+1),\frac{i}{m}(2m+1)\right)
=
\left(2i-2+\frac{i-1}{m},\;2i+\frac{i}{m}\right).
\]
Since \(1\le i\le m\), the left endpoint lies between \(2i-2\) and \(2i-1\), and the right endpoint lies between \(2i\) and \(2i+1\). Thus this brick overlaps exactly the three lower bricks with indices
\[
2i-1,\qquad 2i,\qquad 2i+1.
\]
So from every brick in any layer, there are exactly \(3\) possible moves down to the next layer.

Jessica starts in layer \(1\). To reach layer \(2026\), she must make \(2025\) moves. At each move she has exactly \(3\) choices, and each choice gives a distinct sequence of moves. Therefore the total number of sequences is
\[
\boxed{3^{2025}}.
\]
